Commentary.Commentary: That's it from us then! We now move to Sabina Park, Jamaica for the second Test on 30th July from 2030 IST so do join us for that clash. Until then, goodbye and take care. Cheers!

MAN OF THE MATCH, Ravichandran Ashwin says the Indian fast bowlers bowled really well and he didn't find rhythm in the first innings because he didn't get long spells. Mentions he was speaking to Anil Kumble on the same this morning. Adds that he got a long spell after lunch today which gave him confidence.

Indian captain Virat Kohli admits he didn't know this was India's biggest win outside Asia in terms of innings. Says everyone in the team was eager to play as they had enough practice. Feels scoring wasn't that easy on day 1 as West Indies bowled well. Credits Shikhar Dhawan for batting well as he showed some character. Adds if one has to win a Test then he has to score quickly and give the bowlers time to take wickets. Feels it was a team effort and credits Ashwin. Adds they were going with 5 bowlers so they felt to bring Ashwin at number 6. Mentions they went with three seamers as there was some grass initially and feels there was carry on this wicket. Credits Shami for bowling so well in his comeback game. Adds he's a perfect Test bowler and he's a threat to the opposition. Feels they need to adapt quickly to stay on top and have to be smart always. (On the remaining three games) He says he is confident with the skills they have. Feels they are in a good position as everything came along nicely and shouldn't be complacent.

West Indies captain Jason Holder says India posted a big first innings total as they didn't bowl well. Mentions his batters couldn't get any partnership going and that was disappointing. Adds they need to build some pressure. He will see how Jamaica (pitch) is first and then will decide if they have to make any changes or not. He thinks Jamaica is normally a pretty flat pitch and he'll see it later once he goes there.

Comprehensive win for India as they will take many positives from this huge victory. Their batters got out mostly to poor balls and weren't tested much. Their bowling was terrific overall to take 20 wickets and emerge victorious on day 4. Special mentions once again - Virat Kohli for a sensational double ton and Ravichandran Ashwin first for his century and then for a 7-fer in the second innings.

West Indies' second innings couldn't make any difference either. This time it was Ravichandran Ashwin who ran through the batting line-up. Marlon Samuels and Carlos Brathwaite were the batters who scored fifties as rest of the batters struggled. Bishoo fought hard towards the end but he was only delaying the inevitable. In the end, India registered a big win under their belt.

When you're chasing a huge first innings total, more often than not you'll crumble and the same happened with the hosts. Umesh Yadav and Mohammed Shami's 4-fer apiece was enough to bowl out Windies for a cheap score. Only Kraigg Brathwaite and Shane Dowrich managed to get fifties but it was not enough for them to avoid the follow-on.

What an emphatic win for India! They lead the 4-match Test series 1-0! Biggest win for India outside the subcontinent in Tests. It can't get any better for the visitors. They started the day with needing 9 wickets to win and they were successful enough to take them. They won the toss on day 1 and opted to bat on a wicket which was pretty good to bat on. They made it count by posting a mammoth first innings total. Riding on Virat Kohli's double ton and Ravichandran Ashwin's century along with some useful contributions by Dhawan and Mishra, India declared on 566/8 with the bat.

It will be interesting to see how West Indies reply in the second session. Let's hope the ground is fully dry by then. Join us back in a bit for the second session to catch all the action.

Hello everyone to the coverage of the day 4 of the first Test between West Indies and India at North Sound. The visitors are firmly in control and are eyeing an innings victory here. West Indies will depend on Darren Bravo and Marlon Samuels to save this Test. It looks really difficult for the hosts so let's see how they reply today. Should be another riveting day of Test cricket.
...Day 4, first session...

Kohli will be very happy to see today's proceedings as his bowlers gave him what he wanted and would what them to continue this performance tomorrow, whereas the West Indian batters would look to avoid their previous innings' failure and give a fightback. So that's it from us. Join us tomorrow at 1930 IST for the 4th day's proceedings. Till then, take care! Cheers!

The Indian bowlers came to the party today picking up 10 wickets in a single day. Shami lead the attack from the front followed by Umesh Yadav who got into his rhythm after wayward early spells and clinched 4 wickets each. Ishant didn't look at his best but ended the day with a wicket to his name. Mishra looked the better of the two spinners and was rewarded with a couple of wickets.

Amazing day of Test cricket! India firmly dominated the day. They put West Indies to bat again after having a lead of 343 runs. Kraigg Brathwaite who stood tall in the first innings playing a gritty knock, got out early in the second to a tired shot while Chandrika and Bravo saw the rest of the mini-session through.

Appeal for a leg before! On the pads, Chandrika gets across to play but misses and gets hit on the thigh pad. The umpire turns down the appeal as the ball would have probably gone down the leg side. That will also be STUMPS ON DAY 3!
